basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus; delebo, inquit, hominem quem creavi a facie terrae,'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus; delebo, inquit, hominem quem creavi a facie terrae, ab homine usque ad animantia, a reptili usque ad volucres coeli; poenitet enim me fecisse eos. Humano etenim more dolere dicitur Deus, cum homines quos ipse creavit hosti potius maligno peccando, quam sibi pie vivendo adhaerere considerat, juxta illud Salomonis: Et dolor patris filius stultus (Prov. XIX, 13). Et iterum: Ira patris filius stultus, et dolor matris quae genuit eum (Prov. XVII, 25). Quod autem etiam interitum omnium animantium terrenorum volatiliumque denuntiat, magnitudinem futurae cladis effatur: nam animantibus rationis expertibus, tanquam et ipsa peccaverint, minatur exitium.
